title: Failsafe SLO stabilizer and eviction oscillation dampener
author: Ethan Moore
description:
Motivation: We observed repeated short-lived tenant evictions during regional transients where the SLO enforcer and eviction controller raced to drain resources, causing oscillation and throughput loss for other tenants. This change introduces a lightweight stabilizer layer between the SLO budget allocator and the eviction orchestrator to prevent oscillatory evictions and to provide an emergency 'quiet window' for KV cache syncs during regional reconvergence.

Design summary: Single-process stabilizer that tracks short-term SLO credit delta and applies a dampening multiplier to eviction scores for tenants that have been evicted and re-requested within a short time window. Key features: 1) tenant-weighted exponential decay on penalty scores to avoid deterministic flip-flops; 2) regional slack propagation that allows neighboring healthy zones to advertise spare capacity for short-lived bursts; 3) emergency KV quiet window to suspend aggressive KV drain during region flaps to avoid repeated cache warmups; 4) fast rollback flag and opt-out for customers on Dedicated.

What changed (high level): Added stabilizer service and controller glue, integrated dampener with existing eviction prioritizer, added feature flag (slo.stabilizer.enabled) and an emergency quiet-window (slo.kv_quiet_window_ms) that defaults to 1500ms during detected regional instability. The feature is gated behind a runtime flag for controlled rollout and metrics are exposed under redwood.runtime.stabilizer.*.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (SRE and Runtime) - [x] Unit tests for decay math and prioritizer integration - [x] Integration tests exercising back-to-back evictions under simulated regional packet loss - [x] Load test on perf-canary with tenant-weighted mix - [x] Feature flagged rollout and telemetry verified - [x] Post-merge monitoring runbook added

Testing notes: Local unit tests cover decay curves and boundary conditions (0-60s). Integration harness simulates regional heartbeat loss using the perf-canary network fault injector; observed reduction in eviction churn from median 3 flips/min to 0.2 flips/min in targeted scenario. Canary showed negligible impact on median P95 latency for non-evicted tenants and a 3% improvement in overall successful request rate during the storm window.

Commits summary: (squashed for merge) - Implement stabilizer service and dampener algorithm - Integrate stabilizer with eviction prioritizer and SLO budget allocator - Add feature flag, config defaults, and runtime metrics - Tests: unit, integration, and canary harness adjustments - Docs: rollout runbook and troubleshooting notes

Files changed (high level): - runtime/stabilizer/controller.go (new) - runtime/eviction/prioritizer.go (modified) - infra/config/flags.go (added slo.stabilizer.enabled and slo.kv_quiet_window_ms) - telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml (new metrics) - tests/integration/eviction_stability_test.go (new) - docs/runbooks/slo_stabilizer_rollout.md (new)

Risk and rollback: The stabilizer can be disabled immediately via the slo.stabilizer.enabled flag. If unintended side effects are seen, we will revert the flag and perform a targeted rollback for affected regions. We also added a fast-fail-safe that disables the quiet window if KV drain times exceed a configured threshold to avoid long-lived cache inconsistencies.

Related work: This complements the regional slack propagation work but differs by acting as a short-term dampener rather than a long-lived priority adjustment. Addresses SUP-3421 (customer reported repeated evictions during regional jitter).
